Question:
Use `tests/qa/legend_init_box_handles_labels_accumulation_test.py`, class `TestLegendInitBoxHandlesLabelsAccumulationQA`, method `test_legend_init_box_handles_labels_accumulation_case`. In that test, lines 17-21 create three plot elements with labels: two lines ('Line 1' and 'Line 2') and one rectangle ('Rectangle 1'). Line 26 calls `ax.legend()`, which internally calls `lib/matplotlib/legend.py::Legend._init_legend_box`. Inside `_init_legend_box` (defined at line 837), execution initializes `handles_and_labels = []` at line 855, then enters a for loop at line 871 (`for orig_handle, label in zip(handles, labels):`). Inside this loop, after creating the handlebox (DrawingArea) at line 889 and textbox (TextArea) at line 884, line 898 executes `handles_and_labels.append((handlebox, textbox))` to accumulate the tuple into the list. After the second iteration of this loop completes (i.e., after accumulating the second (handlebox, textbox) tuple), what is the exact state of the `handles_and_labels` list? Specifically, return: (1) the number of accumulated items, (2) whether the list contains DrawingArea objects, (3) whether it contains TextArea objects, and (4) what label will be processed in the next (third) iteration.
